en.title: Adverbs of frequency
en.goal: Use toujours, souvent, parfois, rarement and jamais to say how often you do something.

blocks.title: Adverbs of frequency
blocks.body: From most to least frequent: toujours (always), souvent (often), parfois (sometimes), rarement (rarely) and jamais (never). In French, the adverb usually comes right after the conjugated verb — unlike English, where it usually goes before the verb.
examples: I always read in the evening.

blocks.title: Where to put the adverb
blocks.body: Placing it right after the verb works for any everyday verb — including the leisure verbs you just learned.
examples: We often go out on the weekend.

blocks.title: Jamais needs ne
blocks.body: Jamais (never) works as a negation — so it needs ne before the verb, just like in ne...pas. The full structure is ne...jamais.
examples: He never goes out on Mondays.
